subject: Mutual Action Plan: hosting mode & region decision for BlueOak POC
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference>
To: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@blueoakhealth.com>, Ana Silva <ana.silva@clearmap.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>
Date: 2025-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft MAP & POC eval plan — hosting mode + region decision

Hi Tom / Ana,

Thanks again for the time today. Per our conversation I’m attaching a one-page mutual action plan (BlueOak_MAP_v1.pdf) that lays out the POC milestones, evaluation criteria, and a proposed close timeline. Two small but important asks we need to lock before the technical kickoff next week:

1) Hosting mode decision for the POC: Hosted (fastest to start) vs Dedicated (reserved capacity) vs Private (VPC/on‑prem).
2) Primary region for the POC (we recommend us-east but can support other US regions).

Quick context so we can move the MAP to execution:
- Hosted in us-east: earliest start (~3 business days), lowest operational lift, will use Redwood’s hosted API.
- Dedicated in us-east: ~3–4 week lead (capacity reservation + contract), predictable throughput and data isolation.
- Private (VPC): ~6–8 week lead, required only if you need full customer‑managed network/KMS or air‑gapped controls.

How we propose to proceed in the MAP:
- Week 0: Confirm hosting mode + region and sign mutual action plan.
- Week 1–2: POC setup (credentials, sample datasets, baseline latency/cost tests).
- Week 3–4: Eval run (throughput, latency, regression checks vs quality baseline).
- Week 5: Close decision and next steps (commit to Hosted->Dedicated cadence or Private rollout).

I attached the MAP draft and a short SOC2 snapshot for your security team. Please let me know if anything in the timeline or acceptance criteria is blocking — we can tighten the MAP or add a gating checkpoint for legal/security.

Next step suggestion: Tom, can you confirm preferred hosting mode + region by EOD Tuesday so we can schedule the kickoff for Thursday?

Thanks,
Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Rafael — helpful summary. A couple of quick clarifying questions before we lock the MAP: 

- Data residency: our product team is reviewing PHI surface. If we start on Hosted, can we guarantee that no customer PII ever leaves the us region? We’d need that for HIPAA compliance during the POC.
- Logs/audit: our security team will want to see where audit logs are stored and retention options (short summary OK).
- Costs: can you share a rough delta in unit cost between Hosted and Dedicated for the expected volume (est. 10k tokens/day)?

I’ll loop in our security lead if needed, but want to understand whether Hosted (fastest) is acceptable or whether we must go Dedicated from day one.

—Tom

Tom — thanks for the quick reply. Short answers up front, then proposed MAP tweak: 

- Data residency: yes — Redwood hosted can be locked to a single cloud region (us‑east‑1) for both model execution and token-level logs. We will note that some infrastructure metadata (routing/health checks) may cross regions inside that cloud provider but no customer prompt/response data will be persisted outside the chosen region. I’ll attach a short note our security team maintains.
- Logs/audit: we can provide per-request audit logs and configurable retention (30/90/365 days) for the POC; SOC2 snapshot included.
- Cost delta: rough order — Hosted is ~20–30% higher per‑unit for small volumes because it includes multi-tenant operational overhead; Dedicated amortizes to ~15–25% lower per‑unit for sustained commitments (depends on model size and batching). I’ll get exact estimates from finance if you want numbers for the 10k tokens/day scenario.

Suggested MAP update (to keep momentum):
- Option A (fast path): Start POC on Hosted in us‑east with a gating security checkpoint at the end of Week 1. If security approves, continue Hosted through evaluation; if not, we pivot to Dedicated and push the acceptance timeline by 2–3 weeks.
- Option B (conservative): Provision Dedicated up‑front (adds 3–4 weeks) if BlueOak prefers no contingency.

Action item for you: pick Option A or B and preferred region. If Option A sounds good, we’ll schedule the Week 1 security review as an explicit MAP milestone.

I’ve looped in Priyom (solutions) for the gating checklist and Ana for legal/partner visibility.

Best,
Rafael

Subject: Technical checklist & acceptance criteria for BlueOak POC (gating items)

Hi all — Laura (Solutions Engineering) here. Adding a concise technical checklist so the Week 1 security gate is concrete and actionable. Please see below and I’ve uploaded a checklist to the shared Drive link.

POC gating checklist (Week 1 security review):
- Confirm region lock: deployment pinned to us‑east‑1 for model execution and token storage.
- Data flow diagram: ingress/egress points, third‑party telemetry (if any).
- Audit logs: per‑request exports (CSV/JSON) and retention set to 90 days for POC.
- Encryption keys: Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS; Dedicated/Private can integrate with customer KMS — note if customer KMS required, that pushes to Dedicated/Private.
- HIPAA checklist: Basic controls (access logging, role separation, retention policy) — we will share a short artifact for your security review.

POC acceptance criteria (end of Week 3 eval run):
- Latency: 95th percentile < 450ms for typical prompt mix.
- Throughput: sustain 20 requests/second in burst (with our recommended batching).
- Quality: no regression > 5% against your quality prompts (we’ll run eval harness).
- Cost: projected per‑token cost within the MAP budget line (TBD — Rafael to confirm).

Notes on region recommendation: us‑east‑1 as primary; us‑west‑2 as fallback for DR. If you require data residency in a particular state (e.g., CA), we can examine a geofence but that typically requires Dedicated or Private.

I attached the SOC2 snapshot requested by Rafael to this thread for the security folks. Happy to jump on a 30‑minute call to walk through the gating checklist mid‑week.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.inference

Attachments: SOC2_snapshot.pdf

- Gate: Week 1 security review (90‑day retention, audit logs exported to our S3 staging bucket for review).
